author: Islam Ibrahim - Carrots Team (FSR 1 algorithm by AMD FidelityFX, MIT license)
name: FSR1
shortDescription: Real FPS boost for 3D: AMD FSR 1 upscaling (EASU + RCAS) fully integrated with GDevelop layers, plus an automatic LOD system for every 3D object.
description: AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 1 and an automatic LOD system for GDevelop 3D, working together.

FSR 1: each 3D layer (with its GDevelop effects, SMAA, tone mapping and 2D plane) is rendered at a lower internal resolution and upscaled to the screen with EASU and sharpened with RCAS. The FSR pass is kept after the tone mapping / sRGB OutputPass and composited with premultiplied alpha, so layers below and transparent backgrounds stay correct. It works with several 3D layers, game resolution changes, dynamic resolution and hot reload.

LOD 3D: every 3D object of the scene is tracked automatically. Distances select full detail, a mid-detail geometry, a low-detail geometry, or distance culling. Geometry is simplified on the fly with vertex clustering (cached per scene and per geometry), shadow casting is disabled for distant objects, and hysteresis avoids flickering. Skinned, morphed, instanced, multi-material and custom-shader meshes are safely skipped and only benefit from distance culling and shadow LOD.

Quick start: at the beginning of the scene, use "Enable performance mode (FSR + LOD)" with Quality/Balanced and LOD Auto. It enables FSR on all 3D layers and LOD for all 3D objects, and keeps them enabled in the following scenes. Keep the UI on a separate 2D layer so it stays sharp.

Notes: FPS gains depend on the scene being GPU-bound (fill rate, shading, shadows). FSR is a spatial upscaler: very thin details and text rendered in 3D are softer. Use the comparison view action to tune the quality.
